findings.where: The logo on every view: the large aqueduct mark in the hero, and the nav lockup (the small mark and 'MMM INFRA', the home link), at both widths
findings.fault: The logo appears in colours the client does not use. The arches are drawn in the page's near-black 'cut' (#2A2925), not the logo grey #404040. The 'MMM INFRA' wordmark is near-black, not the logo blue #0070C0. The logo blue appears nowhere on the page, and the palette tile neither gives the logo's colours a job nor declares them logo-only. The granite ground is the reason. The logo blue falls well short of 3:1 against #B8B5AD, so the full-colour logo cannot sit on this ground. Instead of changing the ground or using a version Mark has approved, the logo has been recoloured.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo it is. His brief says the logo stays and is built by the opening animation, and his wordmark has always been blue. A visitor who knows MMM Infra from his current site, his letterhead or LinkedIn would see a dark, different-looking mark and might not connect this page to him. The house rule is never to recolour a logo, and a one-colour version is made only with the client's yes.

findings.where: Minium red across the page: the hero name and role line, the article heading, the 'CINZEL' specimen, the 'M' in the texture tile, the motion sketch's principle words and its easing curve, as well as the 'Write to Mark' tablet
findings.fault: The single accent is spread over every heading and the ornament as well as the action. On the first screen, two lines of very large red capitals are much bigger than the red button below them, so the button is not the one red thing the eye goes to. On the article specimen the heading is red but the one link ('Streamlining the PPP Process…') is not, so there the accent points away from the action.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank visitor scanning for how to contact Mark. The red button is lost in a field of red headings. It also goes against the direction's own card, which says 'one accent only, and it flows to the action'.
